db_evidence.notes: topic_facts:00001439 at time_s=68790 reads 'pause menu: player selects 上清金葫芦 (restores 5% max health per use); character model animates drinking' -- partial textual corroboration of the correct final gourd choice near the true clue_interval, but the two-gourd COMPARISON itself (湘妃葫芦 vs 上清宝葫芦 and their effect text) is not stored verbatim in any SQL table and can only be recovered via clip_qa reading the in-game UI. event_steps at 68490-68520 documents a textually distinct, earlier DECOY gourd-browsing scene ('browses 药王葫芦 and 青玄葫芦...returns to lava fight with muscular humanoid enemy') at a different bonfire before an unrelated multi-armed-boss fight, which is retrievable by SQL/semantic_search and was mistakenly treated as the target scene by 3 of 5 rollouts. event_steps at 68850-68880 ('hooded character approaches tiger boss at wooden shrine; dialogue confrontation begins') corroborates that 68800-68820 is indeed the true immediate pre-Yin-Tiger window.

root_causes: A decoy gourd-comparison scene exists earlier in the timeline (68490-68520s, before an unrelated boss fight) that is semantically and lexically similar to the true target scene (both involve 'browsing/comparing gourds'), and 3 of 5 rollouts' clip_qa calls landed on or included this decoy window, producing the wrong comparison pair.

The gourd comparison pair is not present as text in any SQL/semantic-search table -- it only exists as on-screen UI the visual sub-agent (clip_qa) must read, so any error or scope mistake in choosing which time window to send to clip_qa directly determines the answer's correctness.

Visual sub-agent (clip_qa) instability on the correct window: rollout 3 queried the true 68700-68820 window (as rollouts 1 and 2 did) but returned a third, mutually-inconsistent gourd pair, indicating the UI read itself is not always reliable even when the time window is right.

Rollout 4 spent excessive retrieval effort exploring unrelated time windows (49900-50400, 65800-66400) via run_sql before locating the correct neighborhood, and even after finding the right episodes text, issued clip_qa only on the decoy sub-window, getting both the pair and the final choice wrong.
what_worked: Rollouts 1 and 2 issued clip_qa directly on a window overlapping clue_interval [68800,68820] (68700-68820 and 68700-68850 respectively) without first visiting the decoy scene, and both independently read the same correct pair (上清宝葫芦 vs 湘妃葫芦) and correct final choice (上清宝葫芦), agreeing with the reference answer.

All 5 rollouts correctly narrowed the general time neighborhood (68xxx seconds) using semantic_search/run_sql before invoking clip_qa, showing the coarse retrieval pipeline (episodes/event_steps/topic_facts search) reliably surfaces the right ~hour/segment even when it doesn't pinpoint the exact scene.
transferable_lessons: When a question specifies 'the last time' an event occurred, verify the located scene is the terminal one and not an earlier lookalike occurrence -- cross-check surrounding event_steps text (e.g. what happens immediately after: does it lead into the actual named boss encounter, or a different fight?) before sending that window to clip_qa.

Prefer anchoring clip_qa windows tightly around the true clue_interval rather than a broad multi-scene span; a too-wide window (e.g. 120s spanning two separate gourd-menu screens) increases the chance the visual sub-agent misreads or conflates content from an adjacent unrelated screen.

When multiple UI-comparison screens plausibly match the question's description, use event_steps' narrative context (what boss/NPC appears right before/after) to disambiguate the correct one via SQL before relying on clip_qa, since SQL text distinguishes 'lava fight with muscular humanoid enemy' from 'hooded character approaches tiger boss at wooden shrine'.

Treat a single clip_qa read of a busy multi-screen interval with some skepticism; if time budget allows, a second, narrower clip_qa call to confirm the exact wording of both compared gourd names would have caught rollout 3's inconsistent read.

Avoid burning retrieval turns on semantically-similar but temporally distant windows (e.g. rollout 4's excursions to 49900-50400 and 65800-66400); use the question's own temporal anchor ('last time') plus the clue-adjacent event_steps text (dialogue confrontation with the tiger boss) to jump straight to the correct neighborhood.
